--- title: "Logistic regression with a binary predictor" format: html: df-print: kable toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true --- # Introduction This notebook extends the treatment example from [logistic-regression foundations](logistic-intro.qmd). We focus on the two arms that make a binary treatment predictor: `waitlist` and `therapist-guided`. Our question is: > Among participants in these two arms, how does the estimated probability of > a low post-treatment LSAS score differ for therapist-guided treatment versus > waitlist? The target is the **therapist-guided minus waitlist probability difference**. We will use the corresponding odds ratio to read logistic-regression output, but the probability difference is the primary clinical result. # Packages and data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(here) library(broom) library(marginaleffects) options( marginaleffects_print_omit = c("s.value"), marginaleffects_print_style = ifelse(interactive(), "summary", "tinytable") ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_binary <- read_csv2(here("data", "steps_clean.csv")) |> filter(!is.na(lsas_post)) |> mutate( # The second level is the event modelled by binomial glm(). lsas_post_bin = factor( if_else(lsas_post < 50, "Low", "High"), levels = c("High", "Low") ), trt = factor( trt, levels = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided", "self-guided") ) ) |> filter(trt %in% c("waitlist", "therapist-guided")) |> droplevels() df_binary |> count(trt, lsas_post_bin, .drop = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|trt |lsas_post_bin | n| |:----------------|:-------------|--:| |waitlist |High | 52| |waitlist |Low | 6| |therapist-guided |High | 32| |therapist-guided |Low | 22|
::: ::: `Low` means `lsas_post < 50`; `High` means `lsas_post >= 50`. As in [logistic-regression foundations](logistic-intro.qmd), this is a teaching outcome, not a diagnosis or a remission definition. The factor order makes `High` the first level, so that the binomial model estimates the probability of the second level: a low post-treatment LSAS score. We explicitly make waitlist the reference group. The treatment contrast shown by the coefficient will therefore be therapist-guided minus waitlist. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} levels(df_binary$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "waitlist" "therapist-guided" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} contrasts(df_binary$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` therapist-guided waitlist 0 therapist-guided 1 ``` ::: ::: # A logistic model for two treatment groups For participant $i$, let $Y_i$ indicate a low post-treatment LSAS score. The model is $$ \operatorname{logit}\left[P(Y_i = \text{Low} \mid trt_i)\right] = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\mathbf{1}\{trt_i = \text{therapist-guided}\}. $$ Here, $\beta_0$ is the log-odds of a low score in the waitlist group, and $\beta_1$ is the therapist-guided-versus-waitlist log-odds difference. These are the quantities that `glm()` estimates directly. They are not yet the most clinically intelligible quantities. | Treatment group | Linear predictor | Model-derived probability | |---|---:|---:| | waitlist | $\beta_0$ | $\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\beta_0)$ | | therapist-guided | $\beta_0 + \beta_1$ | $\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\beta_0 + \beta_1)$ | ## Fit and interpret the model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mod_binary_trt <- stats::glm( lsas_post_bin ~ trt, family = binomial, data = df_binary ) p_binary_trt <- avg_predictions( mod_binary_trt, by = "trt", type = "response" ) diff_binary_trt <- avg_comparisons( mod_binary_trt, variables = list(trt = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided")), type = "response" ) or_binary_trt <- tidy( mod_binary_trt, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE ) |> filter(term == "trttherapist-guided") ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Model interpretation The estimated probability of a low post-treatment LSAS score is **10.3%** for waitlist (95% CI **2.5%** to **18.2%**) and **40.7%** for therapist-guided treatment (95% CI **27.6%** to **53.8%**). Compared with waitlist, therapist-guided treatment **increases** the estimated probability by **30.4 percentage points** (therapist-guided minus waitlist = **30.4 percentage points**; 95% CI **15.1** to **45.7 percentage points**). This is an unadjusted contrast within the restricted two-arm sample. The associated therapist-guided-versus-waitlist **odds ratio** is **5.96** (95% CI **2.30** to **17.63**). It is a ratio of the odds of a low score, not a probability ratio and not a 30.4-percentage-point change. ::: ## Display probabilities and the probability difference ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
trt Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
waitlist 0.103 0.0400 2.59 0.00968 0.0251 0.182
therapist-guided 0.407 0.0669 6.09 < 0.001 0.2764 0.538
``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} diff_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
0.304 0.0779 3.9 <0.001 0.151 0.457
``` ::: ::: The estimated probability difference is calculated after transforming the model to the response scale. It answers a different question from the printed log-odds coefficient: how many percentage points higher or lower is the modelled probability in one group than the other? ## Visualise the group probabilities ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_predictions(mod_binary_trt, by = "trt", type = "response") + labs( title = "Estimated probability of low post-treatment LSAS", subtitle = "Waitlist versus therapist-guided treatment; 95% confidence intervals", x = "Treatment group", y = "Probability of low post-treatment LSAS" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](logistic-one-binary-predictor_files/figure-html/plot-binary-treatment-probabilities-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Log-odds and odds ratios The logistic model is linear on the **log-odds** scale. Exponentiating $\beta_1$ gives the therapist-guided-versus-waitlist odds ratio: $$ \exp(\beta_1) = \frac{\text{odds of a low score with therapist-guided treatment}} {\text{odds of a low score with waitlist}}. $$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} or_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|term | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| conf.low| conf.high| |:-------------------|--------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|--------:|---------:| |trttherapist-guided | 5.958333| 0.5124263| 3.483019| 0.0004958| 2.298356| 17.62762|
::: ::: An odds ratio larger than 1 means higher *odds* of a low score in the therapist-guided group. It cannot be read as a percentage-point increase, because the same odds ratio implies different probability differences at different baseline probabilities. Report the model-derived probabilities and their probability difference when the clinical question concerns chances of an outcome. # Summary In this chapter you learned to: - restrict the STePS data to a binary treatment comparison and set waitlist as the reference category; - fit a binary logistic model with `stats::glm(..., family = binomial)`; - report treatment-specific probabilities and the therapist-guided-minus-waitlist probability difference with 95% CIs; and - interpret the associated odds ratio as a ratio of odds rather than a probability difference.
